english: Storey / top floor / attic / furnished loft
keywords: Storey / top floor / attic / furnished loft tabulātum, tabulātī n.; subtēgulāneum, -ī n. tabulātum, tabulātī n. — storey / floor of a building; also boarded flooring; етаж; също дъсчен под . Traupman p. 125; ancient storey sense in Lewis & Short. summum tabulātum — top floor; последен етаж . A natural compositional expression, suitable for the habitable top floor beneath the roof. subtēgulāneum, subtēgulāneī n. — attic / loft room; таван / таванско помещение . Traupman p. 122; Morgan–Owens lists it under furnished attic. “Attic” is a modern application (Traupman). The ancient adjective’s sense is clear: Pliny, NH 36.185 has pavīmenta … barbarica atque subtēgulānea , floors under the roof, i.e. indoors (Lewis & Short: “that is under the roof, = in-doors”). An older Morgan draft called Pliny’s sense uncertain; the passage settles it. Lewis & Short prints sub-tĕgŭlānĕus with a short e against its own tēgula ; the ē of tēgula is kept here. conclāve sub tēctō — room under the roof / loft room; стая под покрива / обитаема таванска стая . Our transparent alternative. The space need not be used for storage. Eāmus sūrsum! — Let’s go upstairs! Да се качим горе! Ascendāmus in summum tabulātum. — Let’s go up to the top floor. Да се качим на последния етаж.

postīcum, postīcī n. — back door (Traupman 122; Plaut., where rēctum ōstium is the front door).
manūbrium jānuae — door handle (Traupman 123); manūbrium, a handle (Cic.).
obserō, obserāre — bolt, lock (Traupman 122; Ter.; Liv.); sera, serae f. — bolt, bar (Varro, LL 7.108; Ov.).
foricula, foriculae f. — window shutter (Traupman 124; Varro, RR 1.59.1).

pater et Theodōrus cum aviā per postīcum in hortum exiērunt — Dad and Theo went out into the garden by the back door with Grandma (Fābula IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis).
Manūbrium jānuae Theodōrus nōn tetigit — Theo did not touch the door handle (Fābula III, Apud avum et aviam).

Pater, jānuā obserātā, antequam lūmen exstingueret, in ephēmeride breviter scrīpsit — Dad bolted the door and, before turning off the light, wrote a few lines in his diary (Fābula VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum).
Foriculīs apertīs, ē fenestrā per tenebrās arborēs cernēbantur — With the shutters open, the trees could be seen from the window in the dark (Fābula I, Iter in Lūsitāniam).
cum pater, trānsennā dēmissā lūmineque exstīnctō — when Dad, after letting down the shutter and turning off the light (Fābula II, Sintra: castellum et puteus).
fenestra ampla, trānsennā jam subductā, arborēs prōspiciēbat — a big window, its shutter already up, looked out on the trees (Fābula III, Apud avum et aviam).

english: Living room / sitting room / artist’s studio / furniture / armchair / sofa
latin: exedra, exedrae f.; supellex, supellectilis f.
keywords: Living room / sitting room / artist’s studio / furniture / armchair / sofa exedra, exedrae f.; supellex, supellectilis f. Ancient Latin Modern room use Descriptive furniture terms exedra, exedrae f. — sitting room / living room; дневна / всекидневна / хол . Classically a room furnished with seats, for conversation: Vitruvius 5.11.2 exhedrae spatiōsae, habentēs sēdēs (so spelt in the Latin Library text), and in Cicero the room where the speakers of a dialogue sit and talk (de Or. 3.17; N.D. 1.15; Lewis & Short). Traupman p. 125 gives it for “sitting room”. The e is short (Greek ἐξέδρα). Use it for the room’s function; summum tabulātum describes its position in the house. Culīnam habet, cubicula, inter quae hospitium est, balneum, lātrīnam, hortum, trīclīnium, exedram — It has a kitchen, bedrooms (among them a guest room), a bathroom, a lavatory, a garden, a dining room and a sitting room (Fābula III, Apud avum et aviam ). Not sessōrium : Traupman (pp. 124–125) gives it for “living room”, but its ancient senses are “seat, stool” (Caelius Aurelianus) and, in a single passage, “dwelling” (Petronius 77.4 vīperae hujus sessōrium ) (Lewis & Short). officīna artificis; officīna, officīnae f.; artifex, artificis m./f. — artist’s studio / workshop; ателие / работилница . Morgan–Owens records the complete studio phrase, citing Levine. supellex, supellectilis f. — furniture / household furnishings collectively; мебели / покъщнина . Ancient collective noun; broader than just tables and chairs. sella bracchiāta; sella, sellae f. — armchair; кресло / стол с подлакътници . Traupman p. 122. torus tōmentō fartus; torus, torī m.; tōmentum, tōmentī n. — sofa, described as a stuffed couch; диван . Traupman p. 125; a descriptive phrase rather than a unique modern furniture taxonomy. Hīc sedēbimus et colloquēmur. — We’ll sit and talk here. Тук ще седим и ще разговаряме.

english: Ground level / basement / terrace / wing / extension / sand pit / lime kiln
keywords: Ground level / basement / terrace / wing / extension / sand pit / lime kiln plānō pede; hypogēum, hypogēī n. Ancient Latin Modern applications plānō pede — at ground level, entered without steps; на нивото на терена . Vitruvius 6.8.1 aedificia quae plānō pede īnstituuntur (Lewis & Short cites the older numbering 6.11); also 7.4.1 conclāvibus, quae plānō pede fuerint . hypogēum, hypogēī n. (also hypogaeum ) — basement, underground vault; сутерен / мазе . Vitruvius 6.8.1 sīn autem hypogēa concamarātiōnēsque īnstituentur, fundātiōnēs eōrum fierī dēbent crassiōrēs . It can also mean a burial vault (Petronius 111.2); on a building site the Vitruvian sense is clear. For Theo, cella subterrānea . Hīc plānō pede intrāmus; illīc dēscendimus in hypogēum. — Here we walk straight in; over there we go down to the basement. Тук влизаме направо; там слизаме в сутерена. Composed. sōlārium, sōlāriī n. — roof terrace, sunny flat roof or balcony; тераса . Lewis & Short: “a part of the house exposed to the sun, a flat house-top, a terrace”; Plautus, Mil. 340 neque sōlārium neque hortum ; Suetonius, Claud. 10.1. The same noun also means a sundial. subdiālia, subdiālium n. pl. — open-air terraces (Pliny, NH 36.186). diaeta, diaetae f. — a suite or wing of rooms, a pavilion (post-Augustan, Lewis & Short); крило / самостоятелна част от къщата . Pliny, Ep. 2.17.20 diaeta est, amōrēs meī, rē vērā amōrēs: ipse posuī ; Suetonius, Claud. 10.1. The same noun also means a medical diet. adstruō (astruō), adstruere, adstrūxī, adstrūctum — build on, add a building to; пристроявам . Columella 1.5.10 cum veterī adstruitur recēns aedificium ; Pliny, Ep. 9.7.4 astruendī . aedificium adstrūctum ; pars domūs nova, veterī adstrūcta — the new wing / extension; пристройка . Avoid āla : in Vitruvius (6.3.4) the ālae are side rooms off the atrium, not wings. arrēctāria et trānsversāria — uprights and crosspieces, Vitruvius’s names for framing members; see the scaffold-members entry . harēnārium, harēnāriī n. — sand pit, a place where sand is dug; пясъчна кариера . Vitruvius 2.4.2 sīn autem nōn erunt harēnāria, unde fodiātur ; also harēnāria, harēnāriae f. (Varro, Cicero). Not the playground sandpit; see the sandbox entry . fornāx calcāria; fornācis calcāriae f. — lime kiln; варница . Cato, Agr. 38.1 fornācem calcāriam pedēs lātam X facitō, altam pedēs XX . For the lime-burner, calcārius , see the builders entry .
